methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Anvil Robotics operates in the Robotics & Manufacturing sector at an undisclosed stage with an undisclosed valuation and total capital raised. The comparable universe consists of 10 peers within the sector: 1 public company (ticker 277810.KQ) and 8 private firms, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

The peer-median valuation method is not applicable to this analysis. A narrow-filter approach—isolating peers at the same stage, adjacent stages, or similar valuation tiers—yielded fewer than three datapoints, the minimum threshold for reliable triangulation. While the sector contains ten robotics companies, none satisfy the clustering criteria necessary to establish a defensible comparable set. An all-sector median would introduce unacceptable distortion given the wide dispersion of stages and valuations across robotics platforms.

Without sufficient narrowly-matched peers, this valuation cannot be triangulated via market multiples at this time. A forward-looking analysis would require either: (1) disclosure of Anvil's stage and financial metrics to enable tighter peer matching, (2) accumulation of additional same-stage robotics transactions, or (3) application of alternative methods such as discounted cash flow or revenue-multiple frameworks using company-specific data. The current comp set lacks the homogeneity required for confident range estimation.
